title: "Positive control: NRF2 activation in lung lines"
author: "Jannik Franken"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
---

## Purpose

Test whether the pipeline (pre-processing, genotypes, design, limma)
recovers a known mutation–metabolite relationship before the main contrasts
are fitted (D18). NRF2 activation by KEAP1 loss or NFE2L2 gain increases
glutathione synthesis, which consumes intracellular glutamate (Okazaki K et
al. Metabolic features of cancer cells in NRF2 addiction status. *Biophys Rev*
2020. doi:10.1007/s12551-020-00659-8, PMID 32112372). Shorthouse et al. (2022)
found glutathione metabolism enriched for KEAP1 and NFE2L2 mutations in the
same data (Appendix Fig S6).

**Expectation, fixed before the fit** (`config.yml: differential.contrasts.nrf2_lung.readouts`):
glutathione ions higher, glutamate lower in NRF2-altered lung lines. The
control counts as passed if the glutathione ions as a set are significantly
higher (one-sided set test, p < 0.05).

**Decision supported:** whether the main contrasts can be fitted with this
pipeline (Phase 4).

## Inputs

- `data/derived/cancer-cell-lines/shorthouse_v1/shorthouse_analysis_v1.rds`
- `config.yml`: `contrast`, `differential.contrasts.nrf2_lung`

## Methods

Lines: lung lines used in models; NRF2 altered if KEAP1 (any protein-changing
variant or homozygous deletion) or NFE2L2 (likely-driver variant) is altered
(D19, D21). Model: limma on the log2 values of all 1096 ions with the design
`~ batch + histology + KRAS + STK11 + TP53 + NRF2` (histology as blocking
factor, D28; moderated t-statistics, empirical
Bayes), BH adjustment over all ions. Readout ions were matched by name. The
glutathione ions were tested as a set with `limma::fry` (self-contained
rotation test; direction "Up"); fry was chosen because the set is small and
pre-specified, and it accounts for the correlation between the ions.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/use_case.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/plotting.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/mutations.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/differential.R"))
config <- load_config()
derived_dir <- uc_dir(config, "derived")
output_dir <- uc_dir(config, "output", "05_positive_control_nrf2")

data <- readRDS(file.path(derived_dir, "shorthouse_analysis_v1.rds"))
contrast <- config$differential$contrasts$nrf2_lung
contrast$description
```

## 1. Lines and design

```{r design}
d <- contrast_lines(data, contrast, config)
X <- contrast_design(d, c(contrast$blocking, contrast$covariates))
c(lines = nrow(d), altered = sum(d$group), unaltered = sum(!d$group), residual_df = nrow(X) - ncol(X))
colnames(X)

# which gene makes a line NRF2-altered
d %>%
    mutate(KEAP1 = altered_status(data, line, "KEAP1", config),
           NFE2L2 = altered_status(data, line, "NFE2L2", config)) %>%
    filter(group) %>%
    count(KEAP1, NFE2L2)
preview_table(d, caption = "Lines of the contrast with group and covariates")
```

## 2. Fit

```{r fit}
result <- fit_contrast(data, d, X)
res <- result$table %>% arrange(P.Value)
c(ions = nrow(res), adj_p_below_0.05 = sum(res$adj.P.Val < 0.05), adj_p_below_0.1 = sum(res$adj.P.Val < 0.1))
preview_table(res, caption = "All ions, NRF2 altered vs not (lung)")

# p-value histogram: a uniform background with a peak near 0 indicates signal
p <- ggplot(res, aes(P.Value)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.025, boundary = 0, fill = uc_palette("ions")) +
    labs(x = "p-value", y = "Ions", title = "p-values of the NRF2 coefficient") +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "p_value_histogram", output_dir, height = 3.5)
p
```

## 3. Pre-specified readouts

```{r readouts}
# readout ions matched by name, with the expected direction
readouts <- bind_rows(lapply(contrast$readouts, function(r) {
    res %>%
        filter(grepl(r$pattern, name, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
        mutate(readout = r$pattern, expected = r$direction)
})) %>%
    mutate(rank = match(feature_id, res$feature_id),
           as_expected = if_else(expected == "up", logFC > 0, logFC < 0)) %>%
    select(readout, expected, feature_id, name, logFC, t, P.Value, adj.P.Val, rank, as_expected, has_imputed_values)
readouts

# set test of the glutathione ions (direction up)
glutathione_ions <- readouts$feature_id[readouts$readout == "glutathione"]
set_test <- limma::fry(result$y, index = list(glutathione = glutathione_ions), design = X,
                       contrast = ncol(X))
set_test
```

```{r volcano, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
p <- res %>%
    mutate(readout = case_when(
        feature_id %in% glutathione_ions ~ "glutathione",
        feature_id %in% readouts$feature_id ~ "glutamate",
        TRUE ~ "other"
    )) %>%
    arrange(readout != "other") %>%
    ggplot(aes(logFC, -log10(P.Value), colour = readout)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = ~ filter(.x, readout != "other"), aes(label = name),
                             size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(glutathione = "#D55E00", glutamate = "#0072B2", other = "grey75")) +
    labs(x = "log2 fold change (NRF2 altered vs not)", y = "-log10 p", colour = NULL,
         title = "NRF2 activation in lung lines",
         subtitle = sprintf("%d vs %d lines; ~ batch + histology + KRAS + STK11 + TP53 + NRF2", sum(d$group), sum(!d$group))) +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "volcano", output_dir)
p
```

```{r readout-values, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
# log2 values of the readout ions per line and group, not adjusted for batch or covariates
p <- as_tibble(data$log2[d$line, readouts$feature_id, drop = FALSE], rownames = "line") %>%
    pivot_longer(-line, names_to = "feature_id", values_to = "log2") %>%
    left_join(select(d, line, group), by = "line") %>%
    left_join(select(readouts, feature_id, name), by = "feature_id") %>%
    mutate(group = if_else(group, "NRF2 altered", "not altered"),
           name = substr(name, 1, 30)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(group, log2, fill = group)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 0.8, alpha = 0.6) +
    facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = uc_palette(c("NRF2 altered", "not altered"))) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "log2 intensity", title = "Readout ions in lung lines (unadjusted values)") +
    theme_uc() +
    theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
save_figure(p, "readout_values", output_dir, width = 8, height = 4)
p
```

## Outputs

```{r save}
out <- c(results = file.path(output_dir, "nrf2_lung_results.tsv"))
readr::write_tsv(res, out[["results"]])
```

## Interpretation

**The positive control passes.**

- 24 NRF2-altered lung lines (19 KEAP1, 5 NFE2L2) were compared with 61
  others, with histology as blocking factor (D28); 17 of 1096 ions have an
  adjusted p < 0.05.
- **All five pre-specified readouts move in the expected direction.**
  Glutathione is higher (log2FC 0.84, adjusted p = 0.005, rank 14 of 1096),
  oxidised glutathione is higher (0.55, adjusted p = 0.11), S-lactoylglutathione
  (0.54, p = 0.08 unadjusted) and cysteine-glutathione disulfide (0.16, not
  significant) as well. The glutamate ion is lower (−0.65, adjusted p = 0.064).
- **The glutathione set is significantly higher** (fry, direction up,
  p = 0.002), which was the pass criterion. Without histology in the model
  (audit/10), glutathione had adjusted p = 0.0015 and the set p = 0.0006.
- None of the readout ions contains imputed values.
- *Not pre-specified, noted for interpretation only:* further ions of the
  glutathione pathway are higher: γ-glutamylcysteine (the product of the
  first step of glutathione synthesis; adjusted p 0.045), cysteinylglycine
  (a glutathione breakdown product; 0.054) and glycine (0.088). The strongest ions
  overall (e.g. glycylproline, nicotinuric acid, orotidylic acid, FAD) were
  not expected and are hypotheses only.

The pipeline recovers the known NRF2–glutathione relationship in this data
set, in agreement with Shorthouse et al. (2022). The main contrasts can be
fitted with the same code.
